title: Find Revenue by City
description: Write a query that returns each customer `city` alongside its total `revenue`, ordered from highest revenue city to lowest - the same three-table join as the top-customers question, just grouped by city instead of by customer.
hints: 💡 SQL concept to consider: same three-table JOIN, different GROUP BY column
The join path is identical to the top-customers-by-revenue query - customers to orders to order_items - only the GROUP BY column changes, from customer_name to city.

SELECT c.city, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS revenue FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id, grouped by city, ordered by revenue descending.
expected_behavior: Returns city and revenue for every city with at least one order, highest revenue first.
solution: SELECT c.city, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS revenue FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id GROUP BY c.city ORDER BY revenue DESC;
explanation: Once you can join customers to order_items through orders, answering "by city" instead of "by customer" is just a one-word change to GROUP BY - the same join, a different lens on the same data.
